idiom_name: System.Text.Json JsonNode DOM with GetValue<T>/Deserialize<T> views
implementation_notes: System.Text.Json ships the document: JsonNode is the base for a mutable DOM and JsonObject implements IDictionary<string, JsonNode?>, so properties are read and written by name; typed views are obtained with GetValue<T>() on a leaf or Deserialize<T>() on a subtree, where a record or class with matching properties plays the trait role. The structure therefore does not have to be hand-written; ExpandoObject with dynamic binding (optionally a DynamicObject subclass) is the other built-in realization when properties are added in code, and the classic hand-rolled dictionary-plus-views form is only justified when views must be shared interfaces across assemblies or storage must be controlled.
code_sketch:
JsonNode doc = JsonNode.Parse(json)!;             // loosely typed document tree
doc["model"] = "300SL";                          // dynamic property
string model = doc["model"]!.GetValue<string>();  // typed view of one property
Car car = doc.Deserialize<Car>()!;                 // typed view of the whole subtree
foreach (var (name, child) in doc.AsObject())      // children traversal
    Console.WriteLine($"{name}: {child}");
pitfalls: The indexer returns null for a missing property and never throws, so a typo turns into a NullReferenceException later; cast to JsonObject and use TryGetPropertyValue when absence is expected.
JsonNode tracks a parent pointer and a node can belong to one parent only, so attaching an already-parented node throws InvalidOperationException - clone the subtree instead.
Careless casting between JsonNode and JsonElement (or re-parsing the same text) silently detaches the value from the DOM, so further edits are lost.

variants.name: ExpandoObject with dynamic member binding
variants.implementation_notes: ExpandoObject is the runtime-shaped document: it implements IDictionary<string, object>, so members can be added and deleted at will, and dynamic binding turns sampleObject.model into a dictionary lookup with a DLR call site behind it. The typed view becomes extension methods or a DynamicObject subclass that projects known keys onto strongly typed members. Choose it for objects built in code (configuration, plugin state) and prefer JsonNode once the document arrives as JSON text.
pitfalls: ExpandoObject is sealed and its members are dynamic: a misspelled member compiles and throws RuntimeBinderException at runtime, and the first dynamic call in a site is slow.
You cannot declare typed members on an ExpandoObject, so a view has to be an extension method or a wrapper and the compiler cannot help either way.
